Here's what the documentation reveals:\n\n## Overview\n\nA write-ahead log or WAL file is used in place of a rollback journal when SQLite is operating in WAL mode. WAL stands for write-ahead logging, and instead of writing changes directly into the main database file and using a rollback journal to undo them on failure, SQLite appends changes to a separate -wal file and periodically merges them back.\n\n## How It Works\n\nWrite-Ahead Logging (WAL) flips this model: changes are appended to a separate WAL file instead of modifying the database file directly. Readers read the original database file while writers append to the WAL file, so readers and writers do not block each other.\n\n## Performance Benefits\n\nUnlike traditional rollback journal modes that lock the entire database for writing, WAL allows reads and writes to proceed concurrently, eliminating a huge bottleneck. WAL mode allows concurrent inserts without blocking reads.\n\n## Enabling WAL Mode\n\nRun PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; once. The setting is persistent - it's stored in the database file header, so future connections automatically use WAL too.\n\n## Checkpointing\n\nCopying data from the wal file into the database file is called a \"checkpoint\", and may be done explicitly (either by \"PRAGMA wal_checkpoint\" or sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()), or automatically (by configuring \"PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint\" - this is the default).\n\nFor the official SQLite documentation, you can refer to the sqlite.org resources, particularly the WAL-mode file format documentation.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."}]}, "parent_tool_use_id": null, "session_id": "e82022dc-cac0-4b54-8c7e-913b6c58f54c", "uuid": "00bdf877-d9d8-4fa7-a53b-a47ab710941e", "timestamp": "2026-09-07T15:00:55.345Z", "tool_use_result": {"query": "SQLite WAL mode documentation", "results": [{"tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01VzBeEF5LsLmXzVHWsb7jmL", "content": [{"title": "Search SQLite Documentation", "url": "https://www.sqlite.org/search?q=wal&i=1"}, {"title": "WAL-mode File Format", "url": "https://www.sqlite.org/walformat.html"}, {"title": "Understanding WAL Mode in SQLite: Boosting Performance in SQL CRUD Operations for iOS | by Mohit Bhalla | Medium", "url": "https://mohit-bhalla.medium.com/understanding-wal-mode-in-sqlite-boosting-performance-in-sql-crud-operations-for-ios-5a8bd8be93d2"}, {"title": "How to Set Up SQLite with WAL Mode on Ubuntu", "url": "https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-02-how-to-set-up-sqlite-with-wal-mode-on-ubuntu/view"}, {"title": "Enabling WAL mode for SQLite database files | Simon Willison\u2019s TILs", "url": "https://til.simonwillison.net/sqlite/enabling-wal-mode"}, {"title": "hctree: Wal2 Mode Notes", "url": "https://sqlite.org/hctree/doc/wal2/doc/wal2.md"}, {"title": "Runnable SQLite Docs: WAL & Concurrency | Coddy", "url": "https://coddy.tech/docs/sqlite/wal-mode-and-concurrency"}, {"title": "Journal Modes in SQLite", "url": "https://blog.sqlite.ai/journal-modes-in-sqlite"}]}, "I've found comprehensive information about SQLite WAL mode.
